reference_memory.normal_pattern: The channel exhibits a piecewise-constant baseline with abrupt upward step transitions, followed by stable plateaus. The dominant motif is a single-step rise occurring roughly one-third into the window, then holding constant for the remainder; this pattern repeats across candidates at different absolute levels. Periodicity is not sinusoidal but defined by the step location relative to window length: in 3-cycle windows (567 points), the step occurs near index ~189 (1/3 of 567); in the 5-cycle window (945 points), it occurs near index ~315 (1/3 of 945), confirming a consistent relative timing (~0.33 window fraction). Baseline levels increase progressively across candidates: ~−1.01 (candidate 0), ~−0.34 (candidate 1), ~+0.34 (candidate 2), ~+0.67 (candidate 3), aligning with the global linear trend (slope ≈ 0.0007–0.0012 per point) inferred from metadata. Amplitude of the step is ~0.67 robust units (e.g., from −0.34 to +0.34 in candidate 2), and plateau values are stable (MAD ≈ 0 in most, except candidate 2 where MAD = 0.337 due to minor quantization or edge effect). Noise is negligible—no visible jitter or high-frequency variation. Boundaries are not truncated; steps occur well within windows. Acceptable variation includes monotonic baseline shift across segments and exact step timing varying by ≤1–2 points; deviations such as multiple steps, downward steps, or noisy plateaus would be anomalous.
